text:
Situation: Lidocaine hydrochloride has been on the FDA drug shortage list since 2012-02-22 and remains Current as of 2026-10-21. Corvale Lakeside holds only 3.9 days of lidocaine hydrochloride 20 mg/mL 50 mL vials (NDC 00143-9575-10). Corvale East holds 18.9 days of the same product. Corvale General holds approximately 6 days across multiple listings.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the shortage on 2012-02-22. An inspection of Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1021343) ended 2010-01-19, classified OAI with six observations on control procedures, in-process specifications, and dissemination of problem information, 764 days before the posting. A Warning Letter was issued to Hospira, Inc. on 2010-04-12, 681 days before the posting. Additional OAI inspections of Hospira, Inc. occurred on 2011-06-17 (250 days before posting) and 2011-08-04 (202 days before posting).

Our position: Internal transfer from Corvale East to Corvale Lakeside is the highest-impact, lowest-risk step to protect Lakeside’s supply while East retains adequate stock. No clinical substitutions are proposed; any therapeutic changes remain with treating clinicians and the committee.

Recommended actions:
1. Approve transfer of 40 vials of lidocaine hydrochloride 20 mg/mL 50 mL from Corvale East to Corvale Lakeside — requires pharmacy director approval of the transfer request.
2. Confirm receipt and update inventory records at both sites — requires pharmacy operations manager approval.
3. Monitor days-on-hand weekly at all three sites and report to P&T at next meeting — requires pharmacy buyer approval.

Not recommended: Purchasing from secondary distributors at premium pricing; initiating therapeutic alternatives without clinician and committee review; transferring stock from Corvale General, which holds only 6 days.
